policy.rule: Separate documented form, published analysis, project inference and unresolved questions. Do not promote similarity to cognacy or a universal sound/morphological law.

evidence_tiers.A: Direct source evidence plus explicit morphological/grammatical analysis on the relevant construction or on both compared endpoints.
evidence_tiers.B: Direct documentary correspondence in form and meaning with source-explicit grammatical support on at least one endpoint; some comparative correspondence remains unresolved.
evidence_tiers.C: Independent formal/semantic triangulation supports a candidate, but morphology or historical identity is not directly established.
evidence_tiers.D: Lexical/grafematic compatibility only; useful as a search target, not as evidence of morphological continuity.
evidence_tiers.N: Negative control or rejected automatic segmentation.

candidates.historical_support: Steffel p.355 documents Cotſchimé ‘Schlafen’ and Cotſchimeameke ‘one who sleeps’; Merrill explicitly analyzes cotschimé-ameke as verbal + participial/adjectival-nominalizing -ameke.
candidates.modern_support: SRC-02 RD-000483 documents Cochí ‘Dormir’ with source-explicit note ‘pp.: cochíami’.
candidates.supports: A very strong cross-temporal candidate for the same lexical-semantic domain and participial function.
candidates.does_not_support: Automatic cognacy of cotschimé and cochí; a general -ameke > -ami law.
candidates.next_source_test: Search independent historical/modern attestations of the ‘sleep’ root and recurrent correspondences for the unresolved root material.

candidates.historical_support: Historical form Tſchiperameke is part of the Steffel comparison set used in the project.
candidates.modern_support: SRC-02 classifies Chipérami ‘Plano’ directly as Pp.
candidates.supports: Formal/semantic candidate strengthened by explicit modern participial classification.
candidates.does_not_support: Cognacy or a direct historical suffix equation without independent root/correspondence control.
candidates.next_source_test: Recover independent attestations of the root and any source-explicit historical derivational analysis.

candidates.historical_support: Steffel documents Rosacameke ‘white’ and rosacame in connected text with the same value; the source also states frequent loss of final ke.
candidates.modern_support: Rarámuri Digital RD-002179 has Rosacami, Adj singular, ‘Blanco’.
candidates.supports: High-priority lexical continuity candidate with same basic color meaning and a direct historical long/short pair.
candidates.does_not_support: That modern -ami necessarily descends from historical -ameke through a universal pathway.
unresolved: modern morphological status beyond lexical classification
candidates.next_source_test: Seek independent color/root attestations that control the final vowel correspondence without selecting forms only for similarity.

candidates.historical_support: Steffel gives Nessé ‘guard/care for’ → Nesséameke ‘guardian’; Merrill also records pouguá nesséameke ‘shepherd of sheep’.
candidates.modern_support: SRC-02 gives Nisé ‘care for/herd’ → Niséami ‘shepherd’; Niséami is classified S rather than Pp.
candidates.supports: Convergence of base meaning, derived agent meaning and specialized pastoral domain.
candidates.does_not_support: Automatic cognacy or an automatic e/é > i/í correspondence.
candidates.next_source_test: Search independent e/é ~ i/í correspondences in comparable lexical environments and additional attestations of the pastoral family.

candidates.historical_support: Steffel Selíameke means a governor/village judge; Merrill documents medial l/r variation elsewhere in the historical material.
candidates.modern_support: SRC-02 Siríami denotes a traditional governor and is classified S; Choguita independently has siˈríame ‘governor(s)’.
candidates.supports: Semantic and cross-variety convergence plus an independently documented historical l/r alternation makes the comparison non-ad-hoc.
candidates.does_not_support: That li in Selíameke is passive -li; that Selíameke and Siríami are established cognates.
candidates.next_source_test: Search independent forms of the governor/govern root and recurrent correspondences in the same phonological environment.

candidates.candidate: tsocamec/otsocamec; ookamek/okamek → tschócameke ~ tschócame → Chócami / modern color forms
candidates.historical_support: Seventeenth-century sources provide black/dark forms in ...amec/...amek; Steffel provides tschócameke ~ tschócame ‘black’.
candidates.modern_support: SRC-02 has Chócami ‘Negro’ as Adj; modern descriptions also contain color morphology involving -ka/-ame in some analyses.
candidates.supports: Strong lexical-semantic and broad formal continuity across several historical layers.
candidates.does_not_support: A backward projection of modern -ka segmentation; identity of final <c>/<k>/<que>/<ke>; explicit modern participial status of Chócami.
unresolved: exact source-to-source lexical identity of all black forms
candidates.next_source_test: Use facsimile/grafematic controls where available and keep lexical continuity separate from morpheme identity.

candidates.historical_support: Merrill explicitly parses tsaní → tsane- → tsane-li- → tsane-li-ameke; this is the unique historical D1 root currently available.
candidates.modern_support: Modern D1 inventory contains ani-lí-ame and rihói-li-ame; ani- also has western controlled attestations anilíame/anilime.
candidates.supports: High-confidence constructional recurrence of internal -li followed by external -ame(ke) across historical and modern documentation.
candidates.does_not_support: Automatic lexical cognacy tsaní ~ ani- or identity of every historical/modern -li function.
unresolved: historical initial consonant correspondence in tsaní ~ ani-
candidates.next_source_test: Test the root relation only through independent correspondences; keep constructional continuity distinct from lexical continuity.

candidates.historical_support: Steffel Tschutschá ‘anoint’ / Tschutschelíla ‘anointing’ / Tschutschelíameke ‘anointed’; Merrill explicitly compares it with parsed tsanelíameke and elsewhere analyzes passive -li before external material.
candidates.modern_support: No direct modern cognate is required for its role as a historical construction control.
candidates.supports: Strong independent historical D2 evidence for X-li-ameke.
candidates.does_not_support: D1 status, because no recovered published morpheme-by-morpheme parse segments this exact token.
candidates.next_source_test: Search source analyses for an explicit parse; otherwise retain D2 strong.

candidates.candidate: machiámec ~ machiámeque ~ machíame; simiámec ~ simíame; atígameque ~ atígame
candidates.historical_support: Tellechea 1826 OCR/source tradition gives same-root long/short participial families; Pimentel independently reports/normalizes parts of the same system and Tellechea explicitly describes final loss/truncation elsewhere in verbal morphology.
candidates.modern_support: Not needed for the internal historical claim.
candidates.supports: High-confidence historical variation/reduction of peripheral material in the ame domain as a general model.
candidates.does_not_support: A single demonstrated direction -ámeque > -ámec > -áme for every participle.
unresolved: exact facsimile reading of critical tokens
candidates.next_source_test: Use facsimile evidence if recoverable; otherwise keep the mechanism high-confidence at the general level and the exact path unresolved.

candidates.historical_support: Merrill analyzes the related ganilíle as ga- + -nilíle, a stative verb.
candidates.supports: Use as a control showing that surface li is insufficient for segmentation.
candidates.next_source_test: None for positive li+ame counting unless new explicit analysis appears.

candidates.historical_support: The base is uilí ‘wait/remain standing’; li belongs to the lexical root.
candidates.next_source_test: None unless an independent analysis contradicts the current root segmentation.

candidates.historical_support: The base is selí ‘govern’; li belongs to the lexical root.
candidates.modern_support: The lexical comparison Selíameke ↔ Siríami remains separately testable as C05.
candidates.supports: Demonstrates why constructional and lexical comparisons must be separated.
candidates.next_source_test: Do not recycle this token as li+ame evidence.

candidates.historical_support: No historical participial -ami was recovered in Steffel.
candidates.modern_support: SRC-02 contrasts huáami (ad.) with huacami (pp.) in the same family; only 20 of 214 final-ami records are classified Pp, while Pp also occurs outside final -ami.
candidates.supports: A direct internal control against automatic morphological tagging from the final string.
candidates.does_not_support: Treating all final -ami as participial or deriving all -ami from historical -ameke.
unresolved: conditioning of modern -ame ~ -ami variation in relevant varieties
candidates.next_source_test: Use source-explicit category/derivational notes, not suffix shape alone.

global_constraints: No automatic segmentation of surface li as passive -li.
No automatic equation of historical <c>, <k>, <que> and <ke>.
No backward projection of modern color -ka into seventeenth-century forms without source control.
No cognacy judgment from graphic similarity alone.
No morphological frequency claim from raw OCR hit counts.
